textbook: Clean cutaway textbook illustration of a SINGLE LYSOSOME — an ORGANELLE inside a eukaryotic cell, NOT a cell and NOT a bacterium — shown at the moment it is FUSING with a phagosome that holds an engulfed bacterium, centred in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with generous negative space around the structures so labels can attach later. Match the exact house look of a refined educational plate: a MUTED, slightly desaturated palette (soft dusty tints, never bright primary or cartoon colours), THIN clean outlines (not heavy black strokes), gentle soft shading, each structure its own distinct soft colour fill. STRUCTURE: a roughly round organelle bounded by EXACTLY ONE thin, smooth, unbroken steel-blue LIMITING MEMBRANE — draw only ONE membrane line, absolutely no second concentric line, no gap, no double membrane anywhere (this single-membrane fact is the single most important point of the picture). Inside, the LUMEN is filled with a warm amber-tan wash, textured and HETEROGENEOUS — never a smooth empty bubble — scattered with small dusty-rose-red granules (the ACID HYDROLASES, digestive enzyme granules, never drawn as scissors or tools) and irregular muted grey-brown chunks (partly digested content). Right beside the lysosome, its membrane visibly MERGING into the lysosome's own membrane at one shared seam, draw a second, separate, pale sky-blue compartment (a PHAGOSOME) containing one simple olive-green rod-shaped ENGULFED BACTERIUM — show the two membranes clearly joining into one continuous boundary at the fusion point, with a few of the rose-red hydrolase granules and teal V-ATPase knobs starting to spill across into the phagosome side. CRITICAL SCIENTIFIC RULES: exactly ONE membrane around the lysosome itself, never two; no cristae (deep membrane folds); no ribosomes studding the outside of the membrane; no stack of flattened membrane discs; do NOT draw a nucleus (no double envelope with pores, no nucleolus, no chromatin) anywhere inside it; the hydrolase enzymes are granules, never literal scissors, knives or tool shapes; the lumen must look granular and heterogeneous, never a smooth empty bubble. Exactly one lysosome and one phagosome in the picture, no duplicates. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, scale bars, arrows or watermarks in the image.
